parts.title: Dark Chocolate's Health-Giving Benefits
parts.article:
A Dark chocolate is gaining a reputation as a heart-healthy food, and research suggests that there might be some substance behind those claims. Ginger Hultin, owner of Champagne Nutrition in Seattle and a spokesperson for the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics says, "Cocoa contains antioxidants in addition to magnesium, potassium, zinc, and iron. Plus, studies have shown that there could be some benefit to consuming chocolate or cocoa for the cardiovascular system, including potentially lowering blood pressure."

B Dark chocolate's health benefits come from its cocoa – specifically its cocoa flavanols. Flavanols are a type of polyphenol, and polyphenols are one group of phytochemicals. Many fruits and vegetables contain flavanols, but they are especially rich in tea, wine, and cocoa. During digestion, cocoa is broken down into smaller chemical compounds. Some research suggests that these compounds have anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties and may help protect against cardiovascular disease, which affects both the heart and brain. For example, research has found that even two weeks of eating dark chocolate or other flavanol-rich cocoa products is better than a placebo for lowering blood pressure in people who already have high blood pressure.

C Not all chocolate is created equal, however. Milk chocolate and white chocolate undergo more processing and contain far less cocoa solids, meaning they have fewer flavanols. Additionally, dairy products added to milk chocolate may interfere with the absorption of antioxidants. To obtain meaningful health benefits, consumers should look for dark chocolate with at least 70% cocoa content. Even then, the exact flavanol content is rarely listed on packaging, as manufacturers have no legal obligation to provide this information. Some specialist brands now produce high-flavanol chocolate, but these products tend to be significantly more expensive than regular dark chocolate.

D The quantity of chocolate needed to produce health benefits has been a matter of debate. Several studies have suggested that consuming 20 to 30 grams of dark chocolate per day – roughly two to three small squares – is associated with the greatest cardiovascular benefits. Consuming more than this amount may add extra calories, sugar, and saturated fat without providing additional protective effects. One large observational study involving over 20,000 participants found that those who ate modest amounts of dark chocolate had a 12% lower risk of developing heart disease compared to non-consumers. However, the same study noted that people who ate chocolate daily also tended to have higher overall calorie intakes and were more likely to be sedentary, suggesting that correlation does not necessarily equal causation.

E Researchers have also investigated dark chocolate's potential effects on cognitive function and mood. A small randomised trial conducted in Italy gave healthy adults either high-flavanol chocolate or low-flavanol chocolate for five days. Those receiving high-flavanol chocolate performed better on visual memory tests and reported feeling less mental fatigue. Similarly, a study from Australia found that regular consumption of dark chocolate was associated with lower odds of clinical depression, though the authors cautioned that people with depression might simply turn to chocolate as a form of self-comfort. Further research with larger sample sizes is needed before firm conclusions can be drawn.

F Despite the promising evidence, experts urge caution against overconsumption. Dark chocolate remains a calorie-dense food, typically containing around 600 calories per 100 grams. Excessive intake can contribute to weight gain, which in turn raises the risk of diabetes, hypertension, and heart disease – the very conditions that moderate consumption may help prevent. Furthermore, some dark chocolate products contain high levels of heavy metals such as lead and cadmium, which accumulate in the body over time and can damage the kidneys and nervous system. Consumer advocacy groups have called for stricter regulation and mandatory testing of heavy metal levels in cocoa products.

G In conclusion, while dark chocolate cannot be considered a medicine, incorporating a small amount into a balanced diet appears to offer genuine health benefits, particularly for cardiovascular health. The key is moderation, attention to cocoa percentage, and awareness of potential contaminants. As Ginger Hultin notes, "Dark chocolate is not a magic bullet, but it can be a pleasant and potentially beneficial part of an overall healthy eating pattern."

reference:
Q14

解析 F段明确提到了某些黑巧克力产品中含有高水平的铅和镉等重金属，且会在体内积累造成损害。

干扰 你可能会去寻找“pollution”或“contamination”这个词，但原文直接用“heavy metals such as lead and cadmium”来具体说明污染问题。

句子 Furthermore, some dark chocolate products contain high levels of heavy metals such as lead and cadmium, which accumulate in the body over time and can damage the kidneys and nervous system. Consumer advocacy groups have called for stricter regulation and mandatory testing of heavy metal levels in cocoa products.

Q15

解析 C段直接建议消费者应该寻找可可含量至少为70%的黑巧克力以获得健康益处。

干扰 你可能在其他段落看到各种数字，但只有C段给出了关于购买“70%”可可含量的具体指导建议。

句子 To obtain meaningful health benefits, consumers should look for dark chocolate with at least 70% cocoa content.

Q16

解析 B段明确举例说明了仅仅两周（短时间内）食用富含黄烷醇的巧克力就能有效降低血压。

干扰 你可能会在A段看到降血压（lowering blood pressure），但A段并没有提到题目中“短期内（within a short period/two weeks）”这个关键的限制条件。

句子 For example, research has found that even two weeks of eating dark chocolate or other flavanol-rich cocoa products is better than a placebo for lowering blood pressure in people who already have high blood pressure.

Q17

解析 E段指出高黄烷醇巧克力能让人的视觉记忆测试表现更好，并且感觉精神疲劳（对应tiredness）减轻。

干扰 你可能会因为没看到“tiredness”原词而卡住，这里原文是用“mental fatigue”做了一对一的同义替换。

句子 A small randomised trial conducted in Italy gave healthy adults either high-flavanol chocolate or low-flavanol chocolate for five days. Those receiving high-flavanol chocolate performed better on visual memory tests and reported feeling less mental fatigue.

Q18

解析 D段提到每天吃巧克力的人通常摄入更多卡路里且更容易久坐，指出了影响他们健康的其他生活习惯。

干扰 你可能会因为题目中的“lifestyle habits”而在全篇寻找“habits”这个词，但原文是用“sedentary（久坐）”和“overall calorie intakes（总卡路里摄入）”来具体表现生活习惯的。

句子 One large observational study involving over 20,000 participants found that those who ate modest amounts of dark chocolate had a 12% lower risk of developing heart disease compared to non-consumers. However, the same study noted that people who ate chocolate daily also tended to have higher overall calorie intakes and were more likely to be sedentary, suggesting that correlation does not necessarily equal causation.

Q19

解析 原文明确列举了可可含有镁、钾、锌和铁（iron）这几种矿物质。

干扰 你可能想填前面的“antioxidants”，但这不属于“如镁、钾、锌”同类的具体矿物质，且题目缺的是并列的最后一项。

句子 Ginger Hultin, owner of Champagne Nutrition in Seattle and a spokesperson for the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics says, "Cocoa contains antioxidants in addition to magnesium, potassium, zinc, and iron.

Q20

解析 原文原句直接说到在消化过程中，可可会被分解成更小的化学化合物（chemical compounds或compounds）。

干扰 不要凭感觉去填“flavanols”，必须严格按照原文中“broken down into smaller”后面的对应词组来填空。

句子 During digestion, cocoa is broken down into smaller chemical compounds.

Q21

解析 原文提到牛奶巧克力中添加的乳制品可能会干扰身体对抗氧化剂的吸收（absorption）。

干扰 你可能会被“interfere with”这个词组迷惑，它完美对应了题目中的“reduce the”，所以直接提取其后的核心名词作答案即可。

句子 Additionally, dairy products added to milk chocolate may interfere with the absorption of antioxidants.

Q22

解析 原文提到一项观察性研究发现，适量食用黑巧克力与降低12%患心脏病（heart disease）的风险有关。

干扰 你可能会填“developing heart disease”，但这超过了两个词的字数限制，只保留核心名词“heart disease”即可。

句子 One large observational study involving over 20,000 participants found that those who ate modest amounts of dark chocolate had a 12% lower risk of developing heart disease compared to non-consumers.

Q23

解析 原文只说了牛奶巧克力和白巧克力的黄烷醇含量都很少，但根本没有比较这两种谁包含的更多。

干扰 不要因为原文把白巧克力和牛奶巧克力放在一起说明就自己脑补它们之间有高低之分，没做比较就是NOT GIVEN。

句子 Milk chocolate and white chocolate undergo more processing and contain far less cocoa solids, meaning they have fewer flavanols.

Q24

解析 原文明确说明制造商“没有法律义务（no legal obligation）”提供黄烷醇含量的标注，这与题目说的“法律要求（legally required）”完全相反。

干扰 你可能会把“no legal obligation”误解为某种特殊的包装规定，做判断题一定要看清“no”这个彻底的否定词。

句子 Even then, the exact flavanol content is rarely listed on packaging, as manufacturers have no legal obligation to provide this information.

Q25

解析 原文明确提到意大利的随机试验给成年人提供了“高黄烷醇巧克力或低黄烷醇巧克力”，证明这两种巧克力都在该研究中被使用了。

干扰 你可能会因为没在原文看到“both”这个词而犹豫，但实验设计的“either... or...”证明研究材料确实包含了这两种巧克力。

句子 A small randomised trial conducted in Italy gave healthy adults either high-flavanol chocolate or low-flavanol chocolate for five days.

Q26

解析 原文建议的最大健康收益摄入量是每天20到30克，并且指出吃更多反而没好处，这与题目说的“至少100克”完全矛盾。

干扰 你可能会在F段的第26句看到“100 grams”这个数字，但那是用来计算黑巧克力卡路里密度的单位，而不是专家推荐的每日摄入量。

句子 Several studies have suggested that consuming 20 to 30 grams of dark chocolate per day – roughly two to three small squares – is associated with the greatest cardiovascular benefits. Consuming more than this amount may add extra calories, sugar, and saturated fat without providing additional protective effects.
